title: Duplicates and blanks
concept:
From here on you work on a **raw export**: the same Aegean orders, but the way a real system hands them over. It has **11 problems of six kinds**, and none of them shows up as an error. Every formula you've learned still runs; it just gives a wrong answer. `=COUNTA(A2:A183)` counts **{{=COUNTA(A2:A183)}}** orders, but the company took 180.

The export sits in columns A–H. The reference tables (Products, Reps, Tiers) are where they always were, in J–X, and they're clean.

**Duplicates.** Exports double up rows when a report is run twice or two files are merged. Spot them with `=COUNTIF(A:A,A2)`: anything above 1 means that ID appears again. Remove them with **Remove Duplicates**. Excel compares only the columns you tick, keeps the first row of each group, and deletes the others.

> [!warn] Tick every column (or the ID column). If you tick only Region, Excel keeps one order per region and deletes the other 170-odd rows. Ctrl+Z undoes it; here, **Undo** does.

**Blanks.** A blank Region isn't a reason to delete an order: it really happened, and its revenue would vanish from every total. Don't guess from the row above either. Look it up from a source that's always right. At Aegean, every order's region is its rep's home region, so a VLOOKUP of the rep's **name** in the Reps table fills it: `=VLOOKUP(E59,$Q$2:$R$8,2,FALSE)`. The table starts at **Q** (RepName), because VLOOKUP searches the first column.

> [!excel] Find blanks: Home ▸ Find & Select ▸ Go To Special ▸ Blanks. Type the formula and press **Ctrl+Enter** to fill every selected blank at once. In the lab, use **Find blanks**, then **Formula fill** with *only the blank ones*.

args.name: A2
args.desc: this row's ID. A result above 1 means it's duplicated

args.name: E2
args.desc: the rep's name on this order

args.name: $Q$2:$R$8
args.desc: RepName → Region, locked so it doesn't drift when filled down
Region is the 2nd column of Q:R

args.name: FALSE
args.desc: exact match: names are IDs here

worked.prompt: Is order O1034 (row 35) in the export more than once?
worked.explain: COUNTIF counts how many cells in column A equal the ID in A35. The answer is **{{=COUNTIF(A:A,A35)}}**: the order appears twice, on rows 35 and 36. Test it in the formula bar: the matches light up green.

mistakes: Remove Duplicates with only a non-ID column ticked (say Region): Excel keeps the first row per region and deletes real orders.
Deleting a row because one cell is blank. The order happened; fill the gap instead.
Filling a blank with a guess (the row above, the most common region). Look it up from a source that's always right.
`=VLOOKUP(E2,$P$2:$R$8,3,FALSE)` with a rep **name**: column P holds RepIDs, so every lookup is #N/A. Start the table at the column you search (Q).

drills.ask: How many times does order **O1121** appear in the export? Type a COUNTIF over the OrderID column in the **Formula fill** bar and press **Test**.
drills.hint: Count the ID in column A: `=COUNTIF(A:A,"O1121")`, or point at one of its cells.

drills.ask: How many orders have an **empty Region**? Count the empty cells of D2:D183 with COUNTIF, and **Test** it.
drills.hint: An empty criterion, `""`, matches empty cells: `=COUNTIF(D2:D183,"")`.

drills.ask: Remove the duplicate orders, keeping one copy of each. Then press **Check**.
drills.hint: Remove duplicates with every column ticked (or just OrderID).

solution.explain: Remove Duplicates with every column ticked.

drills.ask: Fill each empty **Region** with the region of that order's rep, looked up from the Reps table. Then press **Check**.
drills.hint: Formula fill into column D, only the blank cells: `=VLOOKUP(E2,$Q$2:$R$8,2,FALSE)`. Both blank orders belong to the same rep.

solution.explain: =VLOOKUP(E2,$Q$2:$R$8,2,FALSE) filled into the blank cells of D.

questions.prompt: In Remove Duplicates you tick **only Region**. What happens?
options: Excel keeps one row per region and deletes all the others
Only exact duplicate rows are removed
Nothing: Region isn't an ID column
Excel asks which copy to keep
questions.explain: Remove Duplicates treats rows as duplicates when the ticked columns match. With only Region ticked, every order after the first in each region is a "duplicate", and gets deleted.

questions.prompt: An order has an **empty Region**. What's the best fix?
options: Look it up from the rep's home region
Copy the region from the row above
questions.explain: The order is real, so deleting it loses revenue; the row above is a guess. A pivot doesn't ignore it either: it shows a "(blank)" row.

questions.prompt: `=COUNTIF(A:A,A2)` returns **2**. What does it tell you?
options: A2 is on the second row
The ID in A2 appears twice in column A
questions.explain: COUNTIF counts the cells in A:A equal to A2's ID. 2 means the ID appears twice.

claimAfter: I can find and remove duplicate records, and fill blanks from a reliable source instead of guessing.
notYet: You haven't standardised text, fixed numbers stored as text, or corrected typos with Find & Replace yet. That's the next lesson.
